Are they equivalent? 7 includes extra qualifier "by Parliamentary Liberal Party". That adds information not present in 0. The complete proposition of 7 includes that he was leader by the party. 0 does not state that. So they are not equivalent because 7 has extra qualifier. The test: does 0 convey all substantive info of 7? No, missing "by". So not equivalent. Also 13 says Brendan Nelson elected as leader of Parliamentary Liberal Party, point in time 2007 Federal Election. That's different relation (elected as leader of) and object is Parliamentary Liberal Party, not Liberal Party of Australia. So not same.

The core proposition: Abbott is leader of Liberal Party at that time. So they are equivalent. Need to ensure no extra qualifiers: both just date. So group {2,16}. Representative choose clearer; maybe 2.

Now 1: Malcolm Turnbull position held leader of Liberal Party, point in time 16 Sep 2008. No other candidate with same. Not same as 9 (successor) etc.

Since 5 includes that it's the result of 2010 election, 20 lacks that. So not equivalent.

This seems similar to 4/12 but phrasing: result in increase in Liberal Party vote (object "Liberal Party vote"). 4 says election result increase in vote (object "increase in vote") with subject party. 12 says vote increase for party. 18 says election resulted in increase in Liberal Party vote. This is same as 4/12. Does 18 have qualifier? none. But subject is election, same as 12. So 18 also equivalent to group {4,12}. So add 18.

payload.title: Liberal Party of Australia
payload.paragraph_text: Following the 2007 Federal Election, Dr Brendan Nelson was elected leader by the Parliamentary Liberal Party. On 16 September 2008, in a second contest following a spill motion, Nelson lost the leadership to Malcolm Turnbull. On 1 December 2009, a subsequent leadership election saw Turnbull lose the leadership to Tony Abbott by 42 votes to 41 on the second ballot. Abbott led the party to the 2010 federal election, which saw an increase in the Liberal Party vote and resulted in the first hung parliament since the 1940 election.
